data.title: Rising star Aeya's life cut short
data.description: The Thai golf community is mourning the loss of 15-year-old junior golfer Aeyavarin "Aeya" Pradubyart, who passed away following a lightning strike during a junior golf tournament in Chachoengsao on Sunday.

data.title: T1 giants Ratchaburi and Port seek Asian lifelines
data.description: Ratchaburi hope to salvage a point against Vissel Kobe in the AFC Champions League Elite on Tuesday.

data.title: Thai juniors rule world meet at Hua Hin
data.description: Thailand's young golfers claimed several titles at the Singha Thailand Junior World Golf Championship, which concluded at Royal Hua Hin Golf Course in Prachuap Khiri Khan on Sunday.

data.title: PP targets corruption, economic failures
data.description: The opposition has accused the government of monopolising political power, exploiting public funds and failing to address economic pressures and flooding ahead of a proposed censure debate.

data.title: Experts urge deeper ties with Japan
data.description: Experts on Thai-Japan relations say Japan and Thailand should deepen cooperation in advanced manufacturing, clean energy and digital infrastructure to strengthen regional competitiveness and economic resilience.

data.title: Graft claims cast doubt on solar scheme
data.description: The People's Party has called for an investigation into alleged irregularities in the government's 50-billion-baht household solar scheme, including suspected collusion among contractors and alleged kickbacks of 30,000 baht per installation.

data.title: PP urges govt to promote domestic gaming industry
data.description: People's Party MP Pawoot Pongvitayapanu has urged the government to support Thai-owned game development, saying Thailand must capture more value from its 37-billion-baht gaming market.

data.title: Solar scheme promises savings, but at what cost?
data.description: The government's Solar for the People scheme offers households subsidies of up to 50,000 baht to install solar power systems, but consumers should weigh installation costs, eligibility requirements and potential savings before signing up.

data.title: Ministry widens crackdown on industrial waste
data.description: The Industry Ministry will inspect 3,049 factories nationwide that handle industrial waste disposal and recycling, aiming to bring them up to standard within a year, Industry Minister Varawut Silpa-archa said.

data.title: Cabinet to weigh B78.5bn development plan for Isan
data.description: The mobile cabinet meeting in Udon Thani on Tuesday will consider 170 development projects worth more than 78.5 billion baht, covering agriculture, border trade, tourism and drug suppression across five northeastern provinces.

data.title: Amnesty clause may aid Thaksin's bid for B46bn
data.description: A clause in the new amnesty law could give former prime minister Thaksin Shinawatra a route to challenge convictions and seek the return of 46 billion baht in seized assets, a political scientist has warned.

data.title: PP urges migrant labour management reforms
data.description: People's Party (PP) leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut has condemned an attack on a migrant workers' protest leader, calling for reforms to ease registration burdens and curb corruption.

data.title: PM pledges to protect border
data.description: The government has stepped up security along the Thai-Myanmar border after fighting between Myanmar government forces and rebel troops caused damage to homes and injured people on the Thai side.

data.title: Trial of accused USS Cole attack mastermind opens at Guantanamo
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - Jury selection began on Monday in the long-delayed trial of Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri, the accused mastermind of the 2000 attack on the USS Cole warship that left 17 American sailors dead.

data.title: Top Arab-Israeli leader tells AFP opposition must join to oust Netanyahu
data.description: NAZARETH (ISRAEL) - The leader of the largest Arab-majority party in the incoming Israeli parliament told AFP on Monday that it was time for reluctant opposition members to accept "political reality" and join forces to unseat Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

data.title: Caught cold: fridge cyberattack highlights internet gadget weaknesses
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - Cyberattacks affecting supermarket refrigeration systems in several European countries on Monday highlighted the risks associated with connecting industrial equipment to the internet.

data.title: Prayers, anticipation await Pope Leo in Argentine care home
data.description: CLAYPOLE (ARGENTINA) - A home for disabled people on the outskirts of Buenos Aires was full of anticipation as it prepared to receive Pope Leo XIV, amid a growing controversy over state assistance for those with special needs in Argentina.

data.title: Ukraine, Russia see emergency alert systems hacked
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Emergency alert systems in Russia and Ukraine were hit in cyber attacks overnight leading into Monday, with fake warnings of possible nuclear strikes broadcast to users in both countries.

data.title: Belgian PM offers to quit over budget impasse
data.description: BRUSSELS (BELGIUM) - Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever tendered his resignation to King Philippe on Monday over deadlocked budget talks, but the monarch deferred his decision until after a new meeting Friday.

data.title: Russia resumes strikes on Kherson after truce ends
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Russia resumed strikes on the southern Ukrainian city of Kherson on Monday after the end of a local ceasefire in the area -- the longest truce in the war raging between the neighbours since 2022 -- Kyiv said.

data.title: Israel army withdraws after Hebron operation
data.description: HEBRON (PALESTINIAN TERRITORIES) - Israeli troops withdrew on Monday from an area of the occupied West Bank's largest city that they had evacuated of its Palestinian residents, following an attack that killed two soldiers in October.

data.title: ONE Championship: Tawanchai could return in April, Superlek may need nine more months
data.description: Tawanchai PK Saenchai could return to the ring around April 2027, while Superlek Kiatmoo9 may need another nine months to recover from knee surgery, according to ONE Championship boss Chatri Sityodtong.

data.title: Russia-Thai forum eyes $4.5bn
data.description: The second Russian-Thai Investment Forum in Bangkok attracted more than 2,000 participants and over 1,000 companies, representing investment potential of more than US$4.5 billion (152 billion baht).

data.title: Suvarnabhumi set to double passenger capacity
data.description: A new terminal and fourth runway could double Suvarnabhumi airport's annual passenger capacity to 120 million within the next seven years, according to Airports of Thailand's (AoT) fifth development plan for the airport.

data.title: Bangladesh garment workers clash with police protesting higher wages
data.description: ASHULIA — Thousands of Bangladeshi garment workers blocked a major highway and clashed with police on Monday, demanding a monthly minimum wage more than double their current pay, as protests spread across industrial hubs.

data.title: Nike drops chains with 'Jewelry Collection'
data.description: The world's largest sportswear brand is taking its iconic Swoosh beyond sneakers and apparel, venturing into the jewellery market with a new collection of demi-fine accessories for Holiday 2026.

data.title: Limited French school protests resume as holidays end
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - French students returning from autumn holidays blocked some high schools on Monday, determined to reinvigorate a protest movement despite government concessions during the break.

data.title: 'Special express' city bus trial gets mixed reviews
data.description: The trial run of new express bus services with limited stops was plagued by poor communication on Monday, with many Bangkok commuters left wondering why buses were passing them by without stopping.

data.title: Malaysia approves new train line extension to Thai border
data.description: The Malaysian government has approved an extension of its East Coast rail line to the Thai border in Narathiwat province .

data.title: 1,000-vehicle-protest to end at Govt House
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul said on Monday he was not worried about a planned thousand-vehicle protest over economic hardship that will culminate near Government House later this week.

data.title: ALLY unveils Palm Hills, a 20-block walkable district in Bangkok’s Upper East Side
data.description: Starting with a shaded promenade and a 30-rai park, the privately funded plan aims to create one of Asia’s defining neighbourhoods

data.title: TIDLOR: A Decade of Financial Literacy for a Secure Future
data.description: For people working hard to make ends meet, access to a loan can provide much-needed breathing room. Building a more secure financial future, however, takes more than access to funding. It also takes the knowledge to make informed decisions and the confidence to put that knowledge into practice.
